packs.title: Smoky Gateways
packs.promise: Explore Gatlinburg’s park gateway, mountain roads, makers and elevated views across separate outings.

q.s: Trace how the stream changes from the Sugarlands footbridge to Cataract Falls.
st: Use an open trail or NPS route description.
Observe or identify the footbridge and the falls.
Describe one change in the water or surrounding rock.

q.s: Compare a stone chimney remnant and living forest on the Sugarlands Valley Nature Trail.
st: Follow the paved loop or official route photos.
Locate a stone or built trace of former settlement.
Contrast its texture with one living forest feature.

q.s: Choose one craft medium on the Great Smoky Arts & Crafts Community loop and describe how the maker shapes it.
st: Choose an open studio or official maker profile.
Name its material and one visible shaping method.
Sketch or describe how that method changes the raw material.

packs.title: Downtown and River
packs.promise: Follow connected downtown streets, craft spaces and river paths in one or two afternoons.

q.s: Pair two different materials in Arrowmont’s free public galleries.
st: Check an open gallery or current exhibit listing.
Identify two works made from different materials.
Explain how each material affects form or texture.

q.s: Compare sound and movement beside the Little Pigeon River with nearby Parkway traffic.
st: Walk an open River Road segment or use official walking images.
Note one river sound or movement and one nearby street movement.
Describe how a block changes the pace of the town.

q.s: Describe one visible transformation in Ole Smoky Candy Kitchen’s candy-making process.
st: If a demonstration is running, observe from a permitted spot.
Name one change in shape or texture as candy is worked.
Explain what tool or repeated motion causes it.
